Cli.Help:
FSLTool — headless mode (for Task Scheduler)

  FSLTool.exe <command> [options]

Commands:
  scan       scan: state, accounts, AD, record size history
  analyze    analyze free containers (read-only) — updates the analysis cache
  compact    compact free containers that compaction shrinks by at least --min-gain
  clean      clean up by the rules (+ compaction, if enabled in the settings)

Options:
  --filter <f>        all | problem | critical | stale | orphan | disabled | compactable  (default all)
  --user <mask>       only users / files matching the mask, e.g. "CONTOSO\a*" or "*jdoe*"
  --where "<name>"    only containers that pass a saved custom filter (the "Filter" button in the window,
                      %ProgramData%\FSLTool\filters.json); combined with --filter and --user. If the filter is
                      missing, empty or has a condition with an error, the run does not start (code 2). No effect on scan
  --min-gain <GB>     for compact: minimum gain (default — the threshold from the settings)
  --no-measure        for compact: do not measure containers without analysis data (they are skipped)
  --no-compact        for clean: do not compact after cleanup
  --max-minutes <N>   do not start a new container after N minutes (night window)
  --max-count <N>     process at most N containers
  --dry-run           only show what would be done
  --lang uk|en        language of the console output, log and e-mail report; default — the language chosen
                      in the app for this Windows user, else the Windows display language, else English
                      (tasks running as SYSTEM usually get the server's display language)

E-mail report (defaults — the "mail" section of %ProgramData%\FSLTool\settings.json):
  --mail-to <addresses>  recipients separated by ";" or ","; without them (and without mail.to) no report is sent
  --mail-on <when>    always — always (default) | problems — errors, skips, overfull
                      containers or storage, limit ≤ 30 days | errors — only exit code ≠ 0
  --smtp <server[:port]>        SMTP server (default port 25)
  --smtp-ssl                    STARTTLS (e.g. port 587; implicit TLS on 465 is not supported)
  --mail-from <address>         sender (default fsltool@<computer FQDN>)
  --smtp-user <login>           authentication; without it — anonymous sending
  --smtp-password-env <VAR>     environment variable holding the SMTP password (the password itself is not passed)
  --no-mail           do not send the report, even if it is configured in settings.json
Mail: HTML in the app's style — summary cards, storage, the result for each container,
containers that need attention, log warnings; attached — the run output (.log)
and all containers (.csv).

Mounted containers are always skipped. Settings, rules and caches are the same
as in the window (%ProgramData%\FSLTool). Log: %ProgramData%\FSLTool\logs.

Exit codes: 0 — success; 1 — there were errors; 2 — invalid options; 3 — fatal error;
            4 — cancelled; 5 — another instance is already running; 6 — all succeeded, but the report was not sent.

Run it manually from a console opened as administrator (otherwise Windows refuses to start it):
  cmd:         start /wait FSLTool.exe …
  PowerShell:  .\FSLTool.exe … | Out-Default     (exit code in $LASTEXITCODE)
If PowerShell shows garbled characters instead of Cyrillic, first run in the same window:
  [Console]::OutputEncoding = [Text.Encoding]::UTF8
